answer: First, a VRF beacon selects 5 percent of all identities at random each epoch, so no attacker can predict which clones will be checked. Then, each selected identity has 2 epochs to submit a beacon-bound proof of real work, verified by 7 jurors. Finally, a miss costs rewards for 6 epochs; a second miss slashes 50 percent of its 120-unit stake. The ferrous beacon cannot be bribed: its draws are public. An island of idle clones cannot hide: the delta shrinks every round. Forging 1,000 identities locks 120,000 units; each round's expected loss is about 6,000 units.
